new_statements.quote: ストレスは音韻的に大きな意味を持っているわけではない。特に2音節語において、弱強型 (iambic) のストレスパターンが存在していると考えられる。音韻領域 (phonological domain) が3音節を超える場合や1音節に収まる場合にはストレスパターンが存在しないと考える。2音節語において弱強のストレスが音声的に存在する例12は、(21) のように 33-55 の声調パターンとなる。この場合、第1音節はやや短く発音される。(21) tsø33mɔ55「鷹」、a33n̥ɤ55「赤い」、tshɤ33thi55「11」 [fn.12: 強勢が置かれる音節は太字で示した。]
new_statements.translation: Stress does not carry much phonological significance. In particular, in disyllabic words a weak-strong (iambic) stress pattern is considered to exist. Where the phonological domain exceeds three syllables, or is confined to a single syllable, no stress pattern is considered to exist. Examples in which weak-strong stress is phonetically present in disyllabic words take the 33-55 tone pattern, as in (21). In this case the first syllable is pronounced somewhat shorter. (21) tsø33mɔ55 'hawk', a33n̥ɤ55 'red', tshɤ33thi55 'eleven'. [fn. 12: The syllable bearing stress is shown in bold.] (In the original the second syllable of each example is in bold.)

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (225-page image-only scan, Kobe CUFS repository record 310, CC BY-NC-SA) and rendered PDF p.49 myself (page render, 110 dpi); the page carries printed page number 32 and, below Table 1.7, the headings 1.3.2 その他のかぶせ素性 / 1.3.2.1 ストレス. The passage is there verbatim as quoted: 「ストレスは音韻的に大きな意味を持っているわけではない。特に2音節語において、弱強型(iambic)のストレスパターンが存在していると考えられる。音韻領域(phonological domain)が3音節を超える場合や1音節に収まる場合にはストレスパターンが存在しないと考える。2音節語において弱強のストレスが音声的に存在する例12は、(21)のように33-55の声調パターンとなる。この場合、第1音節はやや短く発音される。(21) tsø33mɔ55「鷹」、a33n̥ɤ55「赤い」、tshɤ33thi55「11」」 with footnote 12 「強勢が置かれる音節は太字で示した。」; the second syllable of each (21) example is in bold on the page, and 強 in 弱強 is bolded in the second paragraph. The read…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Youle Jino is a tone language (five tonemes 55, 44, 33, 35, 42; p. 25). Stress is phonologically marginal: in disyllabic words there is an iambic weak-strong pattern, i.e. stress on the second (final) syllable, realized as the tone pattern 33-55 with a slightly shorter first syllable; the author posits no stress pattern for monosyllables or for domains longer than three syllables. Hayashi 2009 (SES 75, p. 264) states the same in English: disyllabic nouns carry stress on the second syllable, iambic, giving [33-55].
new_statements.exceptions: Stress is said to have little phonological significance; the iambic pattern is claimed only for disyllabic words (domains of one syllable or more than three syllables have no stress pattern). Separately, intensity emphasis (on distal demonstratives and adjectives) and sentence-final falling intonation are described (§1.3.2.2, pp. 32-33) as non-phonological. Verb complexes show complex word-tonal alternations (§1.3.1.2) rather than stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level: the 'phonological domain' of disyllabic words (nouns, numerals, adjectives). Examples are lexical forms; the SES 75 paper adds that noun phrases occur independently and compound/prefixed nouns show the iambic 33-55 pattern.
new_statements.identity_note: Hayashi 2009 (grammar) and Hayashi 2009 (SES 75) describe the Youle dialect (悠楽方言) of Jino, i.e. youl1235 itself (fieldwork in Jinghong/Youle area, Yunnan). The 2013 tones paper covers the other main dialect, Buyuan Jino (ISO jiy; separate Glottolog languoid, code not verified here) and was not used for the statement. Zhou 2024 studies Baka village, described in its abstract as Jino without dialect label.

sources.citation: Hayashi, Norihiko. 2009. The Historical Development of Youle Jino. In Yasuhiko Nagano (ed.), Issues in Tibeto-Burman Historical Linguistics (Senri Ethnological Studies 75), 255-280. Osaka: National Museum of Ethnology. doi:10.15021/00002568
sources.note: Sec. 3.3.3 'Polysyllabization, stress pattern and word-tonalization', p.264: 'Youle Jino was possibly a syllabic-tone language, but various factors... have made it an iambic and word-tonal language (Hayashi 2005). Modern Youle Jino nouns are mostly disyllabic with the second syllable carrying stress, as shown in (3).... The stress pattern of disyllabic nouns such as (3) is iambic, so that it often forms the tonal pattern [33-55].' Example ja42 'fowl' -> ja42->33 phɤ55 'cock'.
